text:
Alex Nguyen: Pushed a draft PR to add a termination handler + mixed-capacity changes for preemptible GPU pools. TL;DR: diversify instance types in the launch template, add user-data to run graceful-drain on interruption, and tag instances for billing + pool routing. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 :sparkles:

Maria Lopez: Nice. Can you paste the user-data snippet here? Want to eyeball signal handling and kube cordon/drain steps.

Alex Nguyen: Sure, here's the core part (in the LT user-data):
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# install interruption-watcher
curl -fsSL https://internal-s3/bootstrap/interrupt-watcher.sh | bash
# watcher will call /local-drain when spot signal detected
# register systemd service to call k8s cordon+drain
```
It posts to a local agent that runs: `kubectl cordon $NODE && kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`

Devon Patel: We need to avoid global API rate spikes during mass evictions. watcher should backoff and stagger drains. Also make the drain cmd respect a max-pods threshold.

Alex Nguyen: Agreed. Updated watcher will randomize a stagger window (30-90s) and check `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase==Running | wc -l` before executing. Also added a TTL to avoid repeated drains if later signals are noisy.

Jamal Carter: On the Terraform side, what's changing? I want the plan output before we apply.

Alex Nguyen: Changes in the LT + ASG resource blocks: add `instance_type` list with weights, `mixed_instances_policy` enabled for nodegroups, and tagging keys `x-redwood-pool` & `x-cost-center`. Example plan snippet:
```hcl
resource aws_autoscaling_group "gpu_workers" {
  mixed_instances_policy {
    launch_template { launch_template_specification { ... } }
    instances_distribution { on_demand_percentage_above_base_capacity = 10 }
  }
}
+ resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_lt_v3" {
+  tag_specifications { resource_type = "instance" tags = { "x-redwood-pool" = "preemptible-gpu" } }
+}
```

Maria Lopez: Make sure AMI rotation logic stays intact. We recently had an issue where old AMIs didn't have nvidia drivers pinned and caused boot failures. Any validation in the plan?

Alex Nguyen: Yes, LT now references `data.aws_ami.gpu_base[var.ami_tag]` and we added a plan-time check GH action that runs a smoke VM init using the new AMI in staging region. PR has workflow `ami-smoke-test` that runs on PRs touching AMI refs.

Devon Patel: What about interruption handling for non-AWS clouds (preemptible GCP)? We need provider-agnostic approach — the watcher should be pluggable.

Alex Nguyen: The user-data installs the same watcher but it selects the cloud adapter based on metadata endpoint. Implemented adapters for AWS EC2 instance metadata (`http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data`) and GCE metadata; both POST to the same local drain endpoint.

Jamal Carter: Rollout plan? I don't want to flip the whole fleet at once.

Alex Nguyen: Canary rollout strategy in the PR: update one ASG subset (10% of capacity) in staging cluster, run canary jobs, monitor `node_ready`, `pod_eviction_rate`, and custom latency SLI (p50/p90 model inference). If metrics look good for 2 hours, gradually increase 25% -> 50% -> 100%. Manual gates at each step.

Maria Lopez: Add an automatic fallback: if `pod_eviction_rate` exceeds threshold or model latency regressions > 5% we auto-fallback by switching ASG to on-demand-only policy and toggle a flag in feature-config.

Alex Nguyen: Added a `flipper` runbook entry and a terraform variable `enable_canary_autofail` with default true. Also added alerting in the console dashboard for `preemptible.drain.errors` and `preemptible.evictions_per_min`.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist: PR #482 contains: 1) LT user-data change 2) mixed_instances_policy toggles 3) tagging updates 4) ami-smoke-test workflow 5) watcher binaries checksum. All checks passing: ✅

Devon Patel: One more ask — please ensure we don't lose spot-interruption metrics when instances retire. Add a final hook that ships the instance-level eviction event to metrics before termination.

Alex Nguyen: Done. watcher will POST to /internal/metrics with a delta and we flush to cloudwatch/stackdriver with a 5s timeout.

Maria Lopez: Approving the PR after a quick lint pass. Leaving final apply to Jamal. :thumbsup:

Jamal Carter: I'll run `terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars` in a maintenance window tomorrow 02:00 UTC, and will run the canary apply with monitoring steps documented in the PR. If anything looks off, I'll rollback using the autoscaling policy revert script.

Alex Nguyen: Thanks — assigning postmortem and tagging oncall. I'll ping the docs team to update the runbook.

Devon Patel: Nice work. Small nit: can we add `CostEstimate` labels so FinOps can track delta?

Alex Nguyen: Added `x-cost-estimate: "-8%"` placeholder, actual numbers after canary.

sre-bot: action: PR #482 merged to `staging` at 1812347001 by Alex Nguyen.

Jamal Carter: Merged and canary applied. Monitoring now.

Maria Lopez: Seeing steady numbers so far. No unusual drain storms.

Devon Patel: Marking as resolved in the thread but keeping follow-up todo: create dashboard for mixed-instance cost per-GPU type.

Alex Nguyen: Filed follow-up ticket in infra backlog: INF-3162. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
